issues.legal_issue: Property inherited by a son from his intestate father under the statutory succession scheme is the son’s individual property and is not property of the son’s Hindu undivided family.
material_facts: A father and son had constituted a Hindu undivided family, but partitioned the family business and thereafter carried it on as a partnership; the family house property remained joint.
The father’s credit balance in the partnership represented capital allotted to him on partition and profits accumulated by him, and was his separate property during his lifetime.
The father died intestate, leaving his son and grandsons. The son inherited the credit balance, while the son’s own Hindu undivided family excluded it from its wealth-tax returns.
The Revenue included the balance in the son’s family’s net wealth; the dispute concerned whether the balance belonged to the son individually or to that family.
issues.conclusion: The credit balance devolved on the son in his individual capacity and was not an asset of his Hindu undivided family; it was therefore not includible in that family’s net wealth.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, read with the Class I Schedule, govern intestate succession and override inconsistent pre-existing Hindu law. A living son’s son is not a Class I heir to his grandfather’s property, and the son takes property devolving under section 8 individually, not as karta of his own family. Section 19, which provides that heirs succeeding together take as tenants-in-common rather than joint tenants, supports the statutory departure from the former law. The Court approved Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P. v. Ram Rakshpal, Ashok Kumar; Additional Commissioner of Income-tax, Madras v. P.L. Karuppan Chettiar; Shrivallabhdas Modani v. Commissioner of Income-Tax; and Commissioner of Wealth-Tax, A.P.-II v. Mukundgirji, and rejected the contrary view in Commissioner of Income-tax, Gujarat-I v. Dr. Babubhai Mansukhbhai.

rule.if: wealth_tax_assessment_of_hindu_undivided_family and father_died_intestate and father_owned_property_separately and son_inherited_property and son_was_separated_from_father_by_partition

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment_of_hindu_undivided: A tax assessment determines the net wealth of a Hindu undivided family that includes the inheriting son.
predicates.father_died_intestate: The father died without leaving a will.
predicates.father_owned_property_separately: The property belonged to the father separately during his lifetime.
predicates.son_inherited_property: The son received the property from his father by inheritance.
predicates.son_was_separated_from_father_by_partiti: The son and father had separated their family interests by partition before the father died.

issues.definition: When a son inherits his separately owned father’s property after the father dies intestate, in a proceeding assessing the son’s Hindu undivided family, the rule treats the inherited property as the son’s individual property rather than as family property.

issues.legal_issue: Interest accruing on a business balance owed to a son in his individual capacity is deductible in computing the business income of the son’s Hindu undivided family.
material_facts: The father’s separate credit balance remained in the books of the business after his death and was transferred to the son’s account as inherited property.
Interest accrued on that balance and was credited in the business books.
The son’s Hindu undivided family claimed the interest as a deduction in computing its business income; the Revenue disallowed it on the ground that the payment was made by the son to himself.
The balance belonged to the son individually, rather than to the Hindu undivided family operating the business.
issues.conclusion: The interest was an allowable deduction in computing the Hindu undivided family’s business income because it was payable on a balance belonging to the son individually, not to the family.
issues.legal_principle: The deduction followed from the Court’s conclusion that the inherited balance was the son’s individual property under section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, rather than property of his Hindu undivided family. Interest on that balance was therefore not a payment by the family to itself. The Court did not identify a specific income-tax deduction provision for this conclusion; its determination followed from the ownership characterization and the related succession principles under sections 4 and 8.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_of_hindu_undivided: An income-tax assessment determines the business income of a Hindu undivided family operating a business.
predicates.family_business_owed_balance_to_son_pers: The family business owed a balance that the son held in his individual capacity.
predicates.interest_accrued_on_that_balance: Interest accrued on the balance owed by the family business.

issues.definition: When a family business is assessed for income tax and owes a balance held personally by the son on which interest accrues, the rule treats that interest as deductible in computing the family business’s income.
